newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open sideways, banks up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open sideways, banks up.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed at the open on Friday in light trading but banks rose after DBS announced a 12 percent rise in profit.

The foreign tranches of banks were the main gainers in moderately light volume. DBS foreign topped the list with a 50 Singapore cents gain to S$18.50. The bank's results released Thursday were just a shade below analysts' expectations.
Engineering-based Van Der Horst rebounded from its losses on Thursday. It was up 40 cents to S$5.40.
Index stocks Fraser & Neave and Keppel Corp also gained 10 cents each to S$12.50 and S$10.30 respectively.

Despite disappointing results from the Keppel stable, Keppel Corp is holding well because the poor earnings are being discounted, said one analyst with a local brokerage. "It is still a blue chip and funds like the management."

After about 40 minutes of trading, the Straits Times Industrial index inched up 0.16 point to 2,179.99. Total market volume was a 29 million shares. Gainers were 98 against losers at 41. Early trading saw large cross trades in counters including Thai telecoms firm Total Access, rig-builder Keppel FELS and fruit seller FKTK.
